title: Binomial colength bound for powers of a parameter ideal
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $d\ge0$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_d\in\mathfrak m$, and put $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$. Suppose $\mathfrak m^a\subseteq J$ for some integer $a\ge1$, and that $L=\mathrm{length}_R(R/J)$ is finite [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. If $d\ge1$, then for every integer $i\ge0$ there is a surjective $R$-linear map
$$ (R/J)^{\oplus\binom{i+d-1}{d-1}}\longrightarrow J^i/J^{i+1} $$
whose components multiply by the degree-$i$ monomials in the $x_j$, and for every integer $n\ge1$ both quotients below have finite length and
$$\mathrm{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^n)\le\mathrm{length}_R(R/J^n)\le L\binom{n+d-1}{d}.$$
If $d=0$, then $J=0$, $\mathfrak m^a=0$, $R$ has finite length $L$, and $\mathrm{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^n)=L$ for every integer $n\ge a$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, proof of d-prime(R) >= d(R): degree-i monomial surjections and summation of power-quotient lengths. The d=0 nilpotent case is separated explicitly.

proof.text: First separate $d=0$. The ideal generated by the empty list is $J=0$, so the hypotheses give $\mathfrak m^a=0$ and $\mathrm{length}_R(R)=\mathrm{length}_R(R/J)=L<\infty$. For $n\ge a$, $\mathfrak m^n=\mathfrak m^a\mathfrak m^{n-a}=0$; hence $R/\mathfrak m^n=R$ and its length is $L$. This proves the entire zero-generator case. In the remaining steps assume $d\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, proof paragraph beginning Assume d-prime(R) = d: multiplication by degree-i monomials; explicit expansion of the counting and summation.

proof.text: For $i\ge0$, let $E_i=\{(e_1,\ldots,e_d)\in\mathbf N^d:\sum_j e_j=i\}$ and set $x^e=\prod_jx_j^{e_j}$. Encode $e$ by a row of $i$ stars separated into $d$ consecutive blocks of lengths $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ by $d-1$ bars. This is a bijection with the choices of the $d-1$ bar positions in $i+d-1$ positions, with inverse counting stars between successive bars. Consequently $E_i$ is finite of size $c_i=\binom{i+d-1}{d-1}$. In particular $E_0$ consists of the zero tuple and its monomial is $1$. These are formal exponent tuples: their values in $R$ need not be distinct or nonzero.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, proof paragraph beginning Assume d-prime(R) = d: multiplication by degree-i monomials; explicit expansion of the counting and summation.

proof.text: The monomials $x^e$, $e\in E_i$, generate $J^i$ as an ideal, directly by induction on $i$: for $i=0$, $J^0=R$ is generated by $1$; in $J^{i+1}=J^iJ$, distribute products of finite linear combinations of the degree-$i$ monomials and the $x_j$. Each resulting product $x^ex_j$ has total degree $i+1$, and conversely every degree-$i+1$ monomial has a positive exponent and is of that form. Define $q_i:(R/J)^{\oplus E_i}\to J^i/J^{i+1}$ by $(\overline r_e)_e\mapsto\sum_e r_ex^e\bmod J^{i+1}$. Changing $r_e$ by an element of $J$ changes the sum by an element of $JJ^i=J^{i+1}$, so this is well-defined and $R$-linear. The generating assertion makes it surjective. Enumerating $E_i$ gives the displayed map with $c_i$ components.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, proof paragraph beginning Assume d-prime(R) = d: multiplication by degree-i monomials; explicit expansion of the counting and summation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to the split coordinate sequences $0\to(R/J)^{\oplus t}\to(R/J)^{\oplus(t+1)}\to R/J\to0$: insertion of a zero final coordinate is injective, the final-coordinate projection is onto, and its kernel is exactly that image. Starting with the zero module gives $\mathrm{length}_R((R/J)^{\oplus t})=tL$. For $q_i$ from step 3 use $0\to\ker q_i\to(R/J)^{\oplus E_i}\xrightarrow{q_i}J^i/J^{i+1}\to0$. The same cited additivity gives $c_iL=\mathrm{length}_R(\ker q_i)+\mathrm{length}_R(J^i/J^{i+1})$ in the extended nonnegative integers. Thus $J^i/J^{i+1}$ has finite length at most $Lc_i$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, parameter-ideal paragraph, using Tag 00IV, lemma-length-additive.

proof.text: For each $i\ge0$, the maps $y\bmod J^{i+1}\mapsto y\bmod J^{i+1}$ and $r\bmod J^{i+1}\mapsto r\bmod J^i$ give an exact sequence $0\to J^i/J^{i+1}\to R/J^{i+1}\to R/J^i\to0$: the first is injective, the second is onto, and the second has kernel precisely the classes represented by elements of $J^i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact], $\mathrm{length}_R(R/J^{i+1})=\mathrm{length}_R(J^i/J^{i+1})+\mathrm{length}_R(R/J^i)$. Starting from $R/J^0=0$, induction and step 4 give finiteness and $\mathrm{length}_R(R/J^n)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\mathrm{length}_R(J^i/J^{i+1})\le L\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}c_i$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, parameter-ideal paragraph, using Tag 00IV, lemma-length-additive.

proof.text: The sum is $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\binom{i+d-1}{d-1}=\binom{n+d-1}{d}$ for $n\ge1$. Indeed for $n=1$ both sides are $1$; adding the next summand $\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}$ and using Pascal's identity gives $\binom{n+d}{d}$, the next right-hand side. Pascal's identity follows by separating the $d$-element subsets according to whether they contain a specified last element. Thus step 5 yields $\mathrm{length}_R(R/J^n)\le L\binom{n+d-1}{d}$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, proof paragraph beginning Assume d-prime(R) = d: multiplication by degree-i monomials; explicit expansion of the counting and summation.

proof.text: Finally $x_j\in\mathfrak m$ gives $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and $J^n\subseteq\mathfrak m^n$: every product of $n$ elements of $J$ lies in $\mathfrak m^n$, and so does every sum of such products. The map $p_n:R/J^n\to R/\mathfrak m^n$, $r\bmod J^n\mapsto r\bmod\mathfrak m^n$, is therefore well-defined, $R$-linear and surjective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to $0\to\ker p_n\to R/J^n\xrightarrow{p_n}R/\mathfrak m^n\to0$. It gives $\mathrm{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^n)\le\mathrm{length}_R(R/J^n)<\infty$. Together with step 6 and the maps of step 3 this proves every assertion for $d\ge1$.
